Delete all central edges to get the join X of A_i=Ind(P_(ell_i−1)); the link of central edge i replaces its factor by B_i=Ind(P_(ell_i−2)), with the empty-face join unit for ell_i=1. Cone interiors are disjoint. In a path, deletion of the penultimate vertex leaves a cone and its link is shorter by three. In residue one, the inclusion B_i→A_i has cofiber the suspension of the contractible path complex Ind(P_(3k−2)) for k≥1, and is the identity for k=0. Hence it is a homotopy equivalence: use the homology isomorphism on equal sphere types, including component bijection for S^0. Residue zero has contractible B_i; residue two has contractible A_i. Thus two residue-two factors make all links and X contractible, exactly one yields one suspended exceptional link, and with none the r equivalent link maps cone off X zero, one, or r times. After the first such cone the remaining r−1 attach by null maps. When s=0 the all-unit case is a set of r isolated vertices; the single residue-two case adds a separate cone vertex to a contractible component. For the integral action, a generator of each relevant factor lies in degree k−1, so the augmented join orientation contributes (−1)^k to an equal-arm transposition. Orient link classes using their isomorphisms to the base and orient cones by the apex first. The relative boundary is then the ordinary augmentation on R tensored with the join orientation lattice, so its integral kernel is exactly the claimed signed lattice. The exceptional link index is fixed in the one-residue-two case, and its cone has the same sign character.
